canonical_json_functions.input_shape: JSON-like value; state types are expected to exclude undefined, functions, symbols, cycles, and non-finite values
canonical_json_functions.normalization_order: null/bool/string primitive handling; numbers through canonNumber; arrays recurse in supplied order; object own keys sort by JS UTF-16 lexical order before recursive emission; unsupported values fall back to null text
canonical_json_functions.output_encoding: Canonical JSON text; number zero and non-finite values emit 0, integers use toString, other finite numbers use toPrecision(12)
canonical_json_functions.notes: Undefined/function/symbol are rendered as null rather than preserved as absence; wire validators reject them before authoritative commit. Arrays are never sorted by this function.

ordering_rules.rule: Object keys sort with default JavaScript UTF-16 lexical order; arrays preserve caller order.

Tags sort by tagType; arena tags by tagType then numeric side with counters excluded; modifiers by type ID; held items by bi, type ID, stack count; ball counts by numeric ball type; weather/terrain counters are excluded.
Final core object sorting is explicit; normalized keyed-mon entries sort by canonical entry text; modifier blobs sort by type ID then canonicalized args; arrays preserve order.
Command targets sort numerically by fieldIndex, ownerSeatId, pokemonId.
Command owners deduplicate and sort numerically; terminal and await controls have no owners.
Successor kinds use declared authority-kind domain order; interaction kinds and opaque/address strings use default lexical sorting after deduplication.
The supplied remaining sequence is preserved and occurrence values must be strictly increasing; it is not sorted by control ID.
Account IDs sort by default JS lexical order before dense seat assignment; seat array order then remains fixed.
NFKC/lowercase normalized strings are compared with JS relational UTF-16 order; original strings are returned.
Events, roster, party, and checkpoint arrays are ordered; event owner derives from sequence parity comments/validation.
Checkpoint arrays preserve caller order; sanitization clamps/truncates but does not sort.
Native JSON.stringify preserves object construction/property insertion order and array order; this is transport encoding, not core canonical JSON.
Journal message comparisons use insertion-order JSON.stringify; snapshot mark keys are sorted before JSON.stringify.
Dataset map keys sort numerically; fixed field tuples and list array order are preserved.
Operation ID component order is epoch, owner, kind, pinned sequence, separated by literal colons.
Modifier identity concatenates typeId, className, JSON.stringify(args ?? []), and JSON.stringify(typePregenArgs ?? []) with literal pipes; nested JSON is insertion-order, not core-sorted.
Pending duplicate identity compares digest and native JSON.stringify(nextControl/subsumes), preserving insertion-order structure.
Active diagnostic token labels sort with default lexical order before freezing the snapshot array.

absent_null_rules.rule: Encountered undefined/function/symbol becomes JSON null text, so this function alone cannot distinguish absent from explicit null.
Undefined, non-finite numbers, sparse holes, cycles, symbols/functions, and non-plain objects are rejected before wire entry acceptance.
JSON.stringify/JSON.parse drops undefined object properties before material digest; explicit null survives.
Absent optional fields are omitted; explicit arenaTags: [] remains present; optional form/ability/tera/status/owner fields omit when undefined.
Optional coop/endState/checkpoint/target remain absent when not supplied; target accepts undefined or integer, not an implicit null wildcard.
Absent data/rewardSurface are deliberately normalized to explicit null inside the fixed proposal arrays.
Explicit null domain values encode as * wildcard; omission is a different structural state.
journalHighWater uses nullish default {} before JSON transport round trip; undefined fields are dropped, explicit null is retained.

integer_assumptions.rule: Authoritative revisions, session epoch, membership revision, seats, and connection generation require Number.isSafeInteger; revisions are positive.
Control wave/turn/index/seat/occurrence coordinates require safe integer bounds with per-field positivity/nonnegativity.
Ledger frontiers and bounded revision windows use safe integer values and ascending revision order.
Replay accepts Number.isInteger wave/turn/slot/seq/choice/indices, which is weaker than safe-integer validation.
Operation ID numeric components use Number and Number.isInteger, not Number.isSafeInteger.
Tick/wave/turn and seat bi/partyIndex/pokemonId/array entries are checked with Number.isSafeInteger at the authoritative boundary.
Finite inputs are floor/truncated and clamped for hp/maxHp, stage, status counters, moves PP, arena turns/layers, money, weather, and terrain.
Zero and -0 emit 0; non-finite emits 0 in these helpers; finite fractional values emit toPrecision(12); integer values emit toString.
FNV BigInt is internal only; dex BigInt attributes encode as exact decimal strings in JSON and restore with BigInt.

evidence: Core, turn/learn, and six other Authority V2 adapters implement separate canonical helpers.
faint-replacement canonicalJson has no explicit array branch; turn/learn normalize undefined/non-finite differently from primitive JSON.stringify helpers.
compatibility_risks.impact: A single Rust canonicalizer can silently change a surface digest.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Keep per-surface wire implementations and test each source algorithm independently.

evidence: frame-codec encodeFrameV2, seat-map payload, relay fingerprints, durability messages, report correlation, dex/starter data, and modifierKey use native JSON.stringify.
compatibility_risks.impact: Sorting object keys globally changes existing transport or proposal identity.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Reproduce insertion-order JSON for those rows; use core sorting only where source calls canonicalize.

evidence: Core canonicalize maps undefined to null text; JSON.stringify omits undefined object properties; Authority V2 rejects undefined; cutover freezes by stringify/parse.
compatibility_risks.impact: Raw canonicalization cannot preserve absence versus explicit null.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Apply the source validator/transport round trip before canonical digesting and retain explicit null.

evidence: parseCoopOperationId uses Number.isInteger, while authority entries and engine boundaries use Number.isSafeInteger.
compatibility_risks.impact: An integer outside the JS-safe range can parse through the legacy operation parser.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Do not silently strengthen this compatibility parser; enforce safe range only at source-equivalent callers.

evidence: makeCoopOperationId emits epoch:owner:kind:pinnedSeq and parseCoopOperationId requires four components, despite a stale three-component comment.
compatibility_risks.impact: A port following the comment will produce incompatible IDs.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Use the four-component emitted/parser form as oracle.

evidence: FNV rows consume UTF-16 code units; seat-map SHA-256 consumes UTF-8 bytes; V2 formats add prefixes and canonical-text lengths.
compatibility_risks.impact: One generic Rust hash or UTF encoding changes wire values.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Preserve each algorithm and encoding; do not replace existing wire digests.

evidence: V2 nullable operation/domain fields encode explicit null as * in next-control; omitted fields are structurally different.
compatibility_risks.impact: Conflating missing and null changes control IDs and admission behavior.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Model absent and null separately at the wire boundary.

evidence: next-control validates supplied remaining occurrences as strictly increasing rather than sorting them.
compatibility_risks.impact: Sorting the sequence changes control IDs and ownership projection.

evidence: Proposal admission and lease compare caller-provided fingerprint strings for equality and do not re-canonicalize.
compatibility_risks.impact: Replacing relay JSON fingerprints with a digest breaks duplicate/conflict identity.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Treat existing proposal fingerprints as opaque wire text.

evidence: seatMapId is SHA-256 over a specified UTF-8 insertion-order JSON payload.
compatibility_risks.impact: BLAKE3 or sorted-key JSON changes authenticated membership identity.
compatibility_risks.required_action: Keep SHA-256 and the exact payload; BLAKE3 is only for future non-wire bundles.

compatibility_risks.required_action: Audit any branch-only delta before changing this inventory.
